# Interpreting results {.unnumbered #interpreting-results}

## In phase, quadrature, and amplitude {#rf-components}

The RF reference is (cos(omega t)). A real response is written

$$
R(t)=X(omega)cos(omega t)+Y(omega)sin(omega t).
$$

Here (X) is In phase, (Y) is Quadrature, and

$$
A(omega)=\sqrt{X(\omega)^2+Y(\omega)^2}
$$

is the nonnegative Amplitude. The optional **Add (pi)** controls reverse a displayed signed component; they do not change the calculated amplitude or underlying susceptibility.

## Resonance locations and widths {#resonance-locations-and-widths}

Resonance positions include the selected static field and diagonal pump light shifts. Widths contain optical-pumping, electron-randomization, and spin-exchange contributions. Multiple Zeeman coherences can overlap and produce an asymmetric total curve even when each individual mode is Lorentzian-like.

## Optical signals {#interpreting-optical-signals}

- Fractional transmission is (delta T=delta S_0/S_0).
- (s_i=S_i/S_0) are normalized Stokes parameters.
- Rotation (phi) is the change of the polarization ellipse azimuth.
- Ellipticity (chi) measures the change toward circular polarization.

For a noncircular input beam,

$$
\delta\phi=
\frac{1}{2}
\frac{s_1\,\delta s_2-s_2\,\delta s_1}
{s_1^2+s_2^2}.
$$

Both the [CBOR and LDOR channels](../theory/cbor-and-ldor.qmd) can contribute to (delta s_1) and (delta s_2).

## Comparing weak and physical-pump curves {#weak-versus-physical-curves}

`PumpN weak` shows the direct weak readout. `PumpN` additionally closes dispersive and dissipative Stokes-to-atom feedback. A difference between these curves therefore measures a model prediction, not merely a different normalization.

If physical-pump feedback strongly shifts a peak or creates a shoulder, check path length, density, detuning, intensity, and the reported loop diagnostic. The [limitations chapter](../theory/assumptions-and-limitations.qmd) explains why a strong closed-loop result can be more sensitive than the weak curve.
